citation: "Chicago in 1820." — hand-coloured lithograph, a bird's-eye view from over the lake, lettered "J. Gemmell lith. 157 Lake St. Chicago".
author: J. Gemmell, lithographer, Chicago; the draughtsman is not named
repository: New York Public Library, I. N. Phelps Stokes Collection of American Historical Prints; the copy held in this repository is chicago/reference/images/chicago/chicago_settlement_view_1820.jpg (catalogued in chicago/reference/images/IMAGE_SOURCES.md)
locator: the whole sheet, 1600 x 1187 px in the copy held here; the Kinzie house is right of the road, about x 1060-1180, y 540-600 px
rights_note: Published before 1930 in the United States; NYPL offers it as public domain.
access_notes: Read off the image file itself on 2026-10-15 (T-2498). The lithographer's line is read off the scan; the date is the catalogue's.
what_it_supplies: the house's place: on the north bank east of the forks, across the river from the fort, end-on to the lake
a fenced green on the house's river side with two poplars at its west end, and trees behind it
what_it_does_not_supply: the house in 1812: it claims 1820 and was drawn decades later
any detail of the house: at about 40 px it shows a gabled block and no openings, stacks or piazza
colour: the colouring was added later and is not evidence
note: A retrospective bird's-eye view, useful for the house's setting and nothing finer. It also draws Native people in canoes; nothing of them is built (AGENTS.md, the standing constraint). Its camera and match record are data/reference_views/kinzie_house_1812/gemmell_1820.json.
